laura_sales: Heads-up: health POC asked for a single-page connectivity handoff. Must: preserve client IP for audit, allow TLS inspection inline, explain SNI rewrite risk to their SOC, and provide exact egress IPs/FQDNs they can paste into their firewall. They also want a 2-week cost note for PrivateLink vs peering.

ali_neteng: TL;DR bullets:
- VPC Peering: preserves src IP end-to-end, needs cross-account peering and routing changes. No endpoint hourly fee; possible inter-AZ/regional data charges.
- PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint): fast to provision, creates ENIs in their subnets; traffic to our service commonly NATs to endpoint EIP(s) unless they deploy a proxy. Has endpoint-hour + per-GB processing fees.

cheng_infra: POC options to propose (pick one):
1) PrivateLink + small NLB + reverse-proxy in their VPC -> preserves client via X-Forwarded-For, minimal infra changes on our side.
2) Cross-account VPC Peering -> preserves client src IP natively, best for IP-based ACLs or auditors.
3) Dedicated/private deployment -> supports proxy-protocol or mutual-TLS if they require cryptographic end-to-end with our infra.

security_ops: Important security notes:
- If their TLS-inspector terminates or rewrites SNI, cert pinning and mTLS validation can fail. Recommend they terminate mTLS at their border and use app-layer auth to our API, or request Dedicated where we can configure mTLS.
- Proxy-Protocol v2 to pass original TCP src is available only on Dedicated/Private deployments (not shared hosted API).

ali_neteng: Copy/paste allowlist (replace placeholders):
```
# OUTBOUND allowlist for Redwood POC
# replace <REDWOOD_EIP_1> and <REDWOOD_EIP_2> with EIPs we provide
allow tcp from 10.50.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_EIP_1> 443
allow tcp from 10.50.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_EIP_2> 443
allow udp from 10.50.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_EIP_1> 123  # if NTP required
# If using PrivateLink, ensure the customer's subnet route to the interface ENI(s) is reachable
```

laura_sales: 2-line cost note for their finance approver?

ali_neteng: Cost note: "PrivateLink: small hourly endpoint fee (~$0.02-$0.05/hr) + per-GB processing (~$0.01-$0.05/GB). VPC Peering: no endpoint hour fee but potential cross-AZ/regional transfer costs. For a light 2-week POC (~100GB) expect O($10-100) in data fees; Dedicated requires a capacity pilot (monthly commit)."
